charter.durable_3: Progress is reported truthfully; nothing is claimed unless a record establishes it.
charter.durable_5: Destructive, irreversible or externally visible actions - rewriting history, deleting work, changing access or visibility, publishing, spending someone's account - need identified human approval first.
charter.durable_6: The direction of the product is itself a human decision; narrowing or redirecting what the project is for is a Charter change.

authority.delegated_delivery: Open PRs and merge to main without a human code-review gate when required checks pass on the current subject.
authority.delegated_release: Create and retire tags and releases, and cut releases from verified delivered versions, within the versioning policy recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md.
authority.reserved_non_cosmetic: Any non-cosmetic edit to AUTHORITY.md or CHARTER.md needs authenticated human approval of the proposed revision or a scoped owner override.
authority.reserved_cosmetic: Cosmetic edits - presentation, typos - that do not change meaning may proceed and be reported.
authority.reserved_destructive: Deleting branches, tags, issues or releases, changing repository visibility, transferring ownership, or changing access control settings.
authority.binding_publish: The agent cannot publish as the maintainer without recorded human intent, widen its own scope, or treat a proposal, draft, passing check or successful helper run as acceptance or qualification.

protocol_old.changes_and_merge_protected: Charter, authority or authority controls: all edits need authenticated human approval of the proposed revision or a scoped owner override.
protocol_old.cosmetic_exception: Historical cosmetic exceptions apply until an authorized upgrade; publisher text cannot amend a target Charter.
protocol_old.repeat_init: Explicit migration identifies old/new rules and effective target revision, resolves ownership conflicts and preserves history.

protocol_candidate.changes_and_merge_protected: Same table row as the old pin; unchanged.
protocol_candidate.cosmetic_exception: Same sentence as the old pin; unchanged.
protocol_candidate.upgrade: `init --upgrade <publisher-ref>` six-step migration: reconcile under old rules, stage/compare with per-action delegation and restriction, propose one issue/PR, prepare without blind overwrite, apply within current authority, check and resume.
protocol_candidate.congruence: The grant, Charter and adopted protocol must agree about each affected action. Conflicting delegation/reservation or a local exception to the active rules blocks that action until recognized clarification, amendment or a scoped override; AI judgement cannot resolve it by choosing the more permissive text.
protocol_candidate.declared_delivery_route: Use the outcome's declared delivery route; verification in a development checkout does not establish availability through an advertised package, tag or deployment.
protocol_candidate.pin_status: Status describes the record's identified pin. An upgrade proposal cannot inherit the old pin's active/prepared/qualified claims; retain those as historical evidence.

conflicts.diagnosis: The Charter reads as per-action approval for publishing; the grant delegates release creation/cutting under a versioning policy and reserves only deletion. The texts do not clearly agree.
conflicts.consequence: Under the candidate congruence rule, release publication can be treated as blocked until clarified; existing practice (v0.1.1) relied on the standing delegation.
conflicts.smallest_resolution: Maintainer clarifies in protected AUTHORITY.md (and optionally one Charter line) that the accepted Release delegation is the identified human approval for creating/cutting releases within the recorded versioning policy, and that deleting releases/tags stays reserved.
conflicts.blocked_scope: Release publication authorization only; implementation and merge are unaffected.

clauses: AUTHORITY.md Reserved: cosmetic edits - presentation, typos - that do not change meaning may proceed and be reported.

Old and candidate protocol Changes and merge: all Charter/authority edits need authenticated human approval or a scoped override; historical cosmetic exceptions apply only until an authorized upgrade.
Candidate congruence rule: a local exception to the active rules blocks the action until recognized clarification/amendment/override.
conflicts.diagnosis: The accepted AUTHORITY cosmetic-edit exception is a local exception to the protocol's all-protected-edits rule; publisher text cannot amend the target Charter/authority, so the migration must surface it.
conflicts.consequence: Cosmetic protected edits (including the stale 'proposal pending acceptance' banner) are blocked unless the maintainer recognizes the exception or amends the authority.
conflicts.smallest_resolution: Maintainer records scoped acceptance of the existing cosmetic exception for this migration, or amends AUTHORITY.md to align with the protocol.
conflicts.blocked_scope: Cosmetic Charter/authority edits; candidate bundle installation is unaffected.
